notes: Reusable option sets from the design (§7). A stage uses one with { "archetype": { "id", "dc", "reward" } }: "dc" in a check means the stage's DC, and every gold amount is multiplied by reward. Texts say "they" so any situation can use them.

entries.name: Hostile group
entries.description: Armed people block the way. Fight, slip past, talk, pay, or run.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Settle it with steel. Resolved as one graded check.

critFail.text: The fight goes badly wrong. You break and run, and they loot what you drop.

fail.text: You drive them off, but every one of you is bleeding.

partial.text: They scatter after a short, ugly fight. {actor} takes the worst of it.

success.text: {actor} leads the charge and they flee, leaving a purse behind.

critSuccess.text: A rout. They abandon their camp and their takings.

options.label: Slip past
options.description: Go around them unseen. If they spot you, you face them badly placed.

critFail.text: A branch snaps under {actor}'s boot, right beside their lookout.

fail.text: They spot you halfway past. Now you have to deal with them, badly placed.

partial.text: You slip by, but a strap catches and a purse falls where you can't go back for it.

success.text: You slip past without a sound.

critSuccess.text: You slip past, and {actor} lifts a purse from their camp on the way.

options.label: Parley
options.description: Talk your way through. Failing leaves you on the back foot.

critFail.text: Talk sours into insults, and someone throws a stone.

partial.text: They let you pass, for a toll.

success.text: {actor} talks them down. You pass unharmed.

critSuccess.text: {actor} talks them round entirely. They share their fire and news of the road.

outcome.text: You pay. They count it twice, then wave you through.

options.label: Run
options.description: Turn back and outpace them. Costs breath, maybe blood, maybe a day.

critFail.text: You scatter in a panic, dropping packs and coin.

fail.text: You get away, but only after a long, punishing chase.

partial.text: You outrun them, but the detour costs you a day.

success.text: You break away and lose them in the brush.

entries.name: Someone in need
entries.description: Someone asks for help. Needs a twist on the situation: it means they are not what they seem, and mean you harm. The help options' twists escalate with "@twist", so the twist uses the twist table ("table": true) or names its own "stage" and "opening".

options.label: Help them, no questions
options.description: Your full effort and your trust. The bigger reward; if it's a trick, you walk into it Exposed and take the first hit.

outcome.text: You throw yourselves into it. Afterwards they press coin on you and won't hear no.

twist.text: You were all in, and that was the opening they wanted.

options.label: Help, but stay on guard
options.description: A smaller reward. If it's a trick, you meet it on even footing, or with the Edge if you read them first.

outcome.text: You help, with one eye on the treeline. They thank you with what they can spare.

twist.text: You kept one eye on them, so when it turns, you aren't caught flat-footed.

options.label: Read them first
options.description: Insight shows how likely a trick is, and a great read shows what kind. Misreading them puts you off your next move.

critFail.text: {actor} stares a little too long. They notice, their story hardens, and the read comes out all wrong.

fail.text: {actor} misreads them, and you go on with the wrong idea of what they want.

partial.text: {actor} isn't sure, but has a feel for the odds now.

critSuccess.text: {actor} reads them like a ledger, and knows exactly how to play this.

outcome.text: You walk on. Their voice follows you down the road for a while.

options.label: Take advantage
options.description: Talk them out of what they have. Word may get around.

critFail.text: They see right through you and shout for help. You leave fast, and the story follows you.

twist.text: They see right through you, and they were the dangerous ones.

fail.text: They clutch their things and back away from you.

partial.text: You come away with a few coins and a bad feeling.

twist.text: You come away with a few coins. They were crooks anyway; nobody will miss them.

success.text: You talk them out of their purse.

twist.text: You rob the robbers. They can hardly complain to the watch.
